name: add_tests_items_controller_webmvctest
description: Writes @WebMvcTest/MockMvc tests for an already-correct controller
prompts: The class src/main/java/com/optarena/catalog/CatalogController.java (already implemented, do not modify it; the app's @SpringBootApplication class already exists too) exposes: GET /catalog/ping, which returns HTTP 200 with the plain text body "pong"; and GET /catalog/greet?name=X, which returns HTTP 200 with JSON body {"message": "Hello, X"} (and when the `name` query parameter is omitted, it defaults to "world", i.e. {"message": "Hello, world"}). Write tests for it at src/test/java/com/optarena/catalog/CatalogControllerTest.java using Spring's @WebMvcTest(CatalogController.class) test slice with an autowired MockMvc, covering: (1) GET /catalog/ping returns status 200 and body "pong"; (2) GET /catalog/greet?name=Sam returns status 200 and JSON {"message": "Hello, Sam"}; (3) GET /catalog/greet with no name parameter returns status 200 and JSON {"message": "Hello, world"}.

test_setup_files.mutation_check.py:
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

IMPL = Path('src/main/java/com/optarena/catalog/CatalogController.java')
TEST_CMD = 'mvn -o -q test -Dtest=CatalogControllerTest'
# Each entry is one mutant: a list of (original, replacement) edits applied
# together. Every `original` anchor must appear exactly once in the pristine
# implementation - which also enforces the prompt's "do not modify it".
MUTANTS = [ [ [ "        return \"pong\";", "        return \"pong!\";" ] ], [ [ "\"Hello, \" + name", "\"Hello \" + name" ] ] ]

def run_tests():
    return subprocess.run(TEST_CMD, shell=True).returncode

src = IMPL.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
for group in MUTANTS:
    for old, _new in group:
        assert src.count(old) == 1, (
            f'protected implementation file {IMPL} was modified - the task said not to change it '
            f'(anchor not found exactly once: {old!r})')

rc = run_tests()
assert rc == 0, f'model tests FAILED against the correct implementation (exit {rc})'

try:
    for i, group in enumerate(MUTANTS, 1):
        mutated = src
        for old, new in group:
            mutated = mutated.replace(old, new)
        IMPL.write_text(mutated, encoding='utf-8')
        rc = run_tests()
        assert rc != 0, (
            f'mutation {i} SURVIVED: the tests still pass against a deliberately broken '
            f'implementation, so they do not actually verify the required behavior')
finally:
    IMPL.write_text(src, encoding='utf-8')

print('PASS (tests pass on correct impl and kill all {n} mutants)'.format(n=len(MUTANTS)))
